result.summary: Homer is honoured by the Argives with gifts, a statue and sacrifices. He then recites the Hymn to Apollo at Delos, is made a citizen by the Ionians, and sails to Ios, where he fails to solve the boys' riddle about lice, recalls the oracle of his death, and dies.

scenes.title: Argives honour Homer
scenes.summary: Delighted by his praise of their race, the Argives give Homer gifts, a bronze statue and sacrifices, and carve an inscription on it.

scenes.title: Hymn to Apollo at Delos
scenes.summary: Homer recites the Hymn to Apollo at the great assembly on Delos. The Ionians make him a citizen of every state and the Delians dedicate the poem in the temple of Artemis.

scenes.title: Riddle of the lice and death
scenes.summary: At Ios, old Homer cannot solve the fishing boys' riddle, remembers the oracle, composes his epitaph, slips in clay and dies three days later. He is buried on Ios.
scenes.stakes: Homer's life: the oracle foretold his death at the riddle, and he dies.

notable_quotes.reason: The boys' famous riddle about lice, which Homer could not solve.
Homer's epitaph, summing up his fame as glorifier of heroes.

analysis.text: The passage closes the legendary biography with a fulfilled oracle: Homer's death comes through a riddle he cannot solve, even though he is the greatest poet.
The honours at Argos, Delos and Ios reflect the many cities that claimed Homer and the cult-like reverence given to him.

legacy.text: The tale of Homer dying over the lice riddle became a widely repeated part of ancient Lives of Homer.

fun_facts.text: The Hymn to Apollo cited here is among the Homeric Hymns, which ancient tradition attributed to Homer.

language_notes.text: "Brazen" means made of bronze (brass-like metal); "costly" here means valuable, rich gifts.
Refers to the Trojan War, fought to recover Helen, wife of Menelaus, taken to Troy. Argives were prominent among the Greek besiegers.
"Hellas" is the Greek name for Greece; the Argives are the people of Argos.
The altar of horns at Delos was famous, said to be built from the horns of goats killed by Artemis.
Creophylus is a Chian poet traditionally said to have hosted Homer, so Homer goes to him on Ios.
"Hunters of deep-sea prey" is a grand, mock-heroic way of addressing fishermen.
The oracle, told earlier in the story, warned Homer that he would die when he failed to solve a riddle posed by boys.

context_notes.text: Chios is one of the islands claimed as Homer's birthplace, so the sacrifice there honours his home.
The Ionians were Greeks of the central Aegean coast and islands, who gathered at Delos for festivals of Apollo.
Artemis was Apollo's twin sister, goddess of the hunt; Delos was the birthplace of both.

literary_notes.text: Offering Homer the honours of the deathless gods exaggerates to show how highly the Argives esteemed him.
The paradoxical answer hides its meaning in apparent contradiction, creating the puzzle that Homer cannot solve.
The greatest poet dies from a trivial slip, after being defeated by a children's riddle about lice.
